units.title: Reading comprehension: main idea and explicit information
units.summary: Reading for gist identifies the overall message or communicative purpose; scanning locates specific details. Authentic and adapted texts can include notices, emails, descriptions and short articles.
units.example: In a school announcement, learners first identify its purpose and then locate the event date and venue.
units.pitfall: Assuming the main idea is always the first sentence or translating every word before reading.
units.task: Create a short notice in English and write one gist question and two detail questions.

units.title: Vocabulary in written context
units.summary: Vocabulary meaning can be inferred from surrounding sentences, word families, cognates and discourse clues. Learners should verify whether a familiar-looking word is a false cognate.
units.example: In 'The road was narrow, so only one car could pass', the context suggests that 'narrow' means not wide.
units.pitfall: Treating every English word that resembles a Spanish word as having the same meaning.
units.task: Write two English sentences that allow the reader to infer an unfamiliar adjective.

units.title: Listening comprehension: global and specific meaning
units.summary: Listening for gist focuses on topic and purpose; listening for details identifies names, times, reasons or instructions. Pre-listening predictions and repeated listening with different purposes can support comprehension.
units.example: After hearing a short invitation, students first identify the type of event and then note when it begins.
units.pitfall: Expecting students to understand every word in a first listening.
units.task: Design a two-stage listening task using a short school announcement.

units.title: Listening vocabulary and paraverbal clues
units.summary: Listeners can infer meaning from tone, stress, surrounding words and situation. Paraverbal cues support interpretation but should be considered alongside linguistic evidence.
units.example: When a speaker says 'Be careful!' with urgent intonation near a wet floor, context and tone reinforce the warning.
units.pitfall: Inferring the entire message solely from tone without checking the spoken content.
units.task: Describe an oral situation in which intonation changes how a phrase is understood.

units.title: Verb tenses and modal verbs
units.summary: Verb tenses help situate events in time and aspect. Modal verbs express functions such as permission (may/can), obligation (must/have to) and possibility (might/may). Interpretation depends on context.
units.example: 'You must wear a helmet' expresses obligation; 'It might rain' expresses possibility.
units.pitfall: Assuming that 'must' and 'might' communicate the same degree of certainty or obligation.
units.task: Write three school-context sentences expressing permission, obligation and possibility.

units.title: Communicative and contextualized teaching
units.summary: Meaningful interaction requires a purpose, an audience and opportunities to negotiate meaning. Information-gap tasks, role-play and collaborative problem-solving can promote language use with scaffolding.
units.example: Pairs receive different timetables and must ask questions in English to identify a shared meeting time.
units.pitfall: Using role-play as rote recitation with no information to exchange or decision to make.
units.task: Design an information-gap activity and specify its language objective and support materials.

units.title: Formative assessment in English learning
units.summary: Assessment should align with the intended language skill. Checklists, observation notes, oral performance criteria and self-assessment can provide evidence for feedback and learner reflection.
units.example: After a short oral exchange, students review a checklist on intelligibility, relevant responses and use of target expressions.
units.pitfall: Assessing listening comprehension solely through spelling accuracy when spelling is not the objective.
units.task: Draft three observable criteria for assessing a short English conversation.
